lines.text: ## How it works

The CLI indexes `base...head` and writes a covering skeleton `review.json`: one path per changed file, stub prose, hunk refs. The skill fills interpretation only: title, groups, summaries, attention, lookFor, sources. `validate` checks refs and coverage. `serve` and `export` share one UI and one git payload. Live git wins.

`pregroup` indexes `base...head` and writes a covering draft `review.json`: one group per repeated change, one for mechanical files, and one for the rest, with stub prose and hunk refs. The skill reads the change with `digest` and `show`, regroups the draft, and fills interpretation only. `validate` checks the schema, refs, coverage, and citations. `serve` and `export` share one UI and one git payload. Live git wins.

## What decides pass or fail

Only `validate` and the `case.json` expects (why, parts, groups, size, source kinds, mechanical paths, together, apart, partsTogether, partsApart) change the exit code. The grader is one read-only call per case. It gets the review, the diff of every group, the frozen sources, the commit messages in the range, and the `Must`, `Good`, and `Must not` lists from `expected.md`. It answers yes or no per item with a quote, and marks each document `lookFor` bullet, group `attention` note, focus caption, line note, and file note the review wrote as true or false at head. The case line shows `must 3/4  good 1/2  mustNot 0/3  bullets 2/2 true`. A false bullet is the costly error: the review told the reader something that is not so.

Only a producer failure, `validate`, and the deterministic checks change the exit code. The checks are the `case.json` expects (why, parts, groups, size, source kinds, mechanical paths, together, apart, partsTogether, partsApart) plus three fixed rules: the producer leaves the work tree clean, no `dependsOn` crosses parts, and every source is real: no `transcript` source, a commit source names a commit in the range, and any other source URL is in the frozen set (`scripts/eval/checks.ts`). The grader is one read-only call per case. It gets the review, the diff of every group, the frozen sources, the commit messages in the range, and the `Must`, `Good`, and `Must not` lists from `expected.md`. It answers yes or no per item with a quote, and marks each document `lookFor` bullet, group `attention` note, focus caption, line note, and file note the review wrote as true or false at head. The case line shows `must 3/4  good 1/2  mustNot 0/3  bullets 2/2 true`. A false bullet is the costly error: the review told the reader something that is not so.

The grader does not judge grouping or prose quality. Grouping is checked by `together` and `apart`, and the split into parts by `partsTogether` and `partsApart`. A group with no `part` sits in one unnamed story, so a one-story review fails every `partsApart` pair. Use them for part decisions with one right answer, not for a count range. Prose is linted: em dashes, sentences over 25 words, summaries with more sentences than the skill allows, and summaries that read as a path list. Lints print on the case line and in the report and do not fail the case.

--- a/docs/eval.md

@@ -12,7 +12,7 @@ A `cursor/<model>` producer model (for example `--producer-model cursor/gpt-5.5`
 
 ## What decides pass or fail
 
-Only `validate` and the `case.json` expects (why, parts, groups, size, source kinds, mechanical paths, together, apart, partsTogether, partsApart) change the exit code. The grader is one read-only call per case. It gets the review, the diff of every group, the frozen sources, the commit messages in the range, and the `Must`, `Good`, and `Must not` lists from `expected.md`. It answers yes or no per item with a quote, and marks each document `lookFor` bullet, group `attention` note, focus caption, line note, and file note the review wrote as true or false at head. The case line shows `must 3/4  good 1/2  mustNot 0/3  bullets 2/2 true`. A false bullet is the costly error: the review told the reader something that is not so.
+Only a producer failure, `validate`, and the deterministic checks change the exit code. The checks are the `case.json` expects (why, parts, groups, size, source kinds, mechanical paths, together, apart, partsTogether, partsApart) plus three fixed rules: the producer leaves the work tree clean, no `dependsOn` crosses parts, and every source is real: no `transcript` source, a commit source names a commit in the range, and any other source URL is in the frozen set (`scripts/eval/checks.ts`). The grader is one read-only call per case. It gets the review, the diff of every group, the frozen sources, the commit messages in the range, and the `Must`, `Good`, and `Must not` lists from `expected.md`. It answers yes or no per item with a quote, and marks each document `lookFor` bullet, group `attention` note, focus caption, line note, and file note the review wrote as true or false at head. The case line shows `must 3/4  good 1/2  mustNot 0/3  bullets 2/2 true`. A false bullet is the costly error: the review told the reader something that is not so.
 
 The grader does not judge grouping or prose quality. Grouping is checked by `together` and `apart`, and the split into parts by `partsTogether` and `partsApart`. A group with no `part` sits in one unnamed story, so a one-story review fails every `partsApart` pair. Use them for part decisions with one right answer, not for a count range. Prose is linted: em dashes, sentences over 25 words, summaries with more sentences than the skill allows, and summaries that read as a path list. Lints print on the case line and in the report and do not fail the case.
